## Context / Problem
The advisory `sweep (windows)` job fails 84 tests in tests/unit/test_review_bot.py (scheduled run 41230936309, ref 0886e96f03a; run 40797257532 shows the same 84). 81 fail with `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests`, 2 with `State object has no attribute 'config'`, and 1 (`test_sigkill_during_a_store_write_orphans_the_mkdir_lock`) with `module 'signal' has no attribute 'SIGKILL'`. The default `_current_revision` stub from eastmost-uncheered-nematode (688e564ff91) did not change this.

Root cause (evidence in the first comment): on Windows, `socket.socketpair()` is the stdlib's `socket._fallback_socketpair`, which connects an AF_INET loopback pair inside the process. Every new asyncio event loop builds its self-pipe that way (`ProactorEventLoop._make_self_pipe`). The autouse network guard in tests/conftest.py (`_guard_socket_connect`) refuses every AF_INET connect, so `asyncio.run`, and any TestClient lifespan, fails before test code runs. A macOS simulation that installs the fallback as `socket.socketpair` reproduces 83 of the 84 failures exactly; the remaining one is the POSIX-only SIGKILL test. Commit 5697f2e1117 already set the rule that local IPC (AF_UNIX) passes the guard because it never touches the network; the in-process loopback pair is the Windows form of that IPC.

## Approach
1. In tests/conftest.py, let `_guard_socket_connect` pass an AF_INET/AF_INET6 connect only when its direct caller is the stdlib socketpair fallback, identified by the caller frame's code object being `socket._fallback_socketpair.__code__` (on Python 3.11 the Windows fallback is `socket.socketpair` itself, so its code object is included too; on POSIX `socket.socketpair` never calls connect, so including it allows nothing new). Every other AF_INET/AF_INET6 connect, including a loopback connect from test or product code, stays blocked. No new fixture, marker, environment variable, or patch is added; the guard's docstring states the exemption and the reason.
2. In tests/unit/test_review_bot.py, mark `test_sigkill_during_a_store_write_orphans_the_mkdir_lock` with `pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", reason=...)`, the precedent used in tests/unit/test_bridge_runner_spawn.py, with a reason naming SIGKILL and the fcntl lock leg as POSIX-only, and add `import os` to the module-level imports (the module does not import `os` today, and the decorator reads `os.name` at collection). The test body is unchanged.
3. Leave `test_lifespan_cancel_await_is_bounded_for_a_task_slow_to_cancel` (rewritten in 782aa2921f6) unchanged; it fails on Windows only through the same event-loop path.

Rejected: switching tests to `WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy` (the selector loop also builds its self-pipe with `socket.socketpair()`, so it hits the same guard); allowing every loopback connect (widens the guard to any local server, which 5697f2e1117 did not intend).

## Scope
- tests/conftest.py: the caller-frame exemption in `_guard_socket_connect` and its docstring.
- tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py: regression tests.
- tests/unit/test_review_bot.py: the module-level `import os` and the POSIX-only skip on the SIGKILL test.
No production code under src/ changes.

## Testing
Regression tests in tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py, run under the autouse guard on every platform:
- `socket._fallback_socketpair()` returns a connected pair that carries bytes both ways. Fails before the fix with the guard's RuntimeError.
- With `socket.socketpair` monkeypatched to `socket._fallback_socketpair` (the Windows configuration), `asyncio.run` of a trivial coroutine completes. Fails before the fix at `_make_self_pipe`.
- Teeth: a plain AF_INET connect from test code to a listening 127.0.0.1 socket in the same process still raises the guard's RuntimeError, so the exemption is not a loopback allowance. The existing TEST-NET-3 test keeps covering a remote address.
Also run tests/unit/test_review_bot.py and the review-bot sibling modules with and without the scratch Windows-simulation plugin, then `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The point where the RuntimeError escapes on Windows is identified and recorded on this ticket.
- [x] The 2 allowance tests (fallback socketpair, asyncio.run on the fallback) fail on the code before the fix.
- [x] The loopback teeth test fails against a deliberately over-broad variant of the fix that allows every loopback connect (temporary edit, reverted).
- [x] The 3 regression tests above pass after the fix.
- [x] With the scratch plugin that installs `socket._fallback_socketpair` as `socket.socketpair`, tests/unit/test_review_bot.py has 0 failures on macOS (it had 83 before the fix).
- [x] Without the plugin, tests/unit/test_review_bot.py has 0 failures on macOS.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] [non-codebase] The first scheduled `sweep (windows)` job after the fix logs zero network-guard RuntimeError tracebacks, and every remaining review-bot failure in it is attributed to a separately tracked ticket.
  provenance: GitHub Actions run 41282090856, job 124775894326 (`sweep (windows)`, head d8801e4dda4): 0 guard tracebacks (364 before the fix); 6 remaining review-bot failures are the pytest 9.2.0 State.config cases tracked by zodiacal-rockbound-egret.
  provenance: the GitHub Actions run id and its result, recorded on this ticket.
